question: In which isochores are Alu elements enriched?

supports.quote: the vast majority of Alu sequences were shown to have the highest density in GC-rich isochores
Alu retrotransposons do not show a homogeneous distribution over the human genome but have a higher density in GC-rich (H) than in AT-rich (L) isochores
The frequency of Alu sequences also increases with increasing GC, but attains a maximum in H2 isochores, in agreement with previous experimental data
The results indicate that the short repeats of the B1 family of mouse and of the Alu I family of man are most frequent in the heavy components

initial_executor.limitations: Evidence e10 notes Alu frequency in introns is roughly equal across isochore classes, contrasting with genomic density trends. Specific isochore classes (H2) are mentioned as having maximum frequency, while general GC-rich or H isochores are described as having higher density.

The frequency of Alu sequences also increases with increasing GC, but attains a maximum in H2 isochores, in agreement with previous experimental data

The results indicate that the short repeats of the B1 family of mouse and of the Alu I family of man are most frequent in the heavy components, whereas the long repeats of the BamHI family of mouse and of the Kpn I family of man are mainly present in the two light components.

same_evidence_Qwen.limitations: Evidence e10 notes Alu elements are found at roughly equal frequencies in introns from all isochore classes, suggesting context-specific distribution; 'heavy components' in e11 refers to buoyant density fractions which correlate with GC-rich isochores but are distinct terminology.
